clue.text: One of two leading characters in AEschylus' oeuvre

definitions.text: One of two leading characters in AEschylus' oeuvre

parts.words: One of two leading characters in AEschylus' oeuvre
parts.note: the first two letters of the Greek dramatist's name, A and E, run together as a single vowel sound, so the 'leading characters' are letters, not roles in his plays

explanation.surface: A question about which of two protagonists dominates the tragedies of Aeschylus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading characters' suggests heroes of Greek drama, but it means the opening letters AE, a vowel pair glided into one sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Two vowels pronounced as one gliding sound form this phonetic unit, as AE often does.

clue.text: Derek briefly had to go on foot in China

parts.note: Del is the short form of the name Derek

explanation.surface: A man called Derek went on foot across China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but means porcelain; DELFT is tin-glazed earthenware from the Dutch town.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is glazed pottery, and china here means crockery or porcelain generally.

clue.text: Discourage dangerous way to put out chip-pan fire

definitions.meaning: the idiom means to dampen enthusiasm for an idea

definitions.text: dangerous way to put out chip-pan fire
definitions.meaning: literally dousing a burning pan of oil with water, which makes it flare dangerously

explanation.surface: Advice that dousing a burning chip pan with water is a hazardous idea.
explanation.walkthrough: A chip pan is a British deep pan of oil for frying chips; water thrown on burning oil makes it explode.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to dampen someone's enthusiasm, just as discourage does.

clue.text: Edit clueing device to cope with temporary problem

annotationWithheld.why: Edit clueing device to cope with temporary problem (4,4): a self-referential clue where 'clueing device' both supplies OVER and acts as the reversal turning TIDE into Edit; one phrase doing two jobs, and the whole-phrase reverse reading is refused
annotationWithheld.clue: Edit clueing device to cope with temporary problem

clue.text: Wielding mop, daily's been employed for four years

indicators.note: a mop being wielded is swung about, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; a daily is also a British cleaner, hence the mop

explanation.surface: A cleaner with a mop has been in the job for four years.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' is a British term for a cleaning lady, which explains the mop in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece the period between successive Games, four years, was an olympiad.

clue.text: Worked hard, taking foundation course?

definitions.meaning: past tense of grind, to toil
the base layer on which a structure or painting rests

explanation.surface: Someone toiled away while studying on an introductory course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foundation course' suggests a college year, but it is the base coat or soil beneath things.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground is the past tense of grind, to slog, and also the base layer underneath anything.

clue.text: Tolerate daughter's hair extension

parts.note: to bear something is to tolerate it
d is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent puts up with their daughter's hairpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair extension' suggests salon wefts, but whiskers are hair extending from the chin.
explanation.definitionFit: Facial hair growing down from the chin is playfully called an extension of hair.

clue.text: Tell the violinist!

parts.note: William Tell, the Swiss hero, shot an apple with an arrow, and a violinist plays with a bow, so both are bow users

explanation.surface: An instruction to pass a message on to the fiddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like a verb but is William Tell, the legendary archer; a violinist also wields a bow.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer shooting arrows and a player drawing a bow across strings both handle a bow.

clue.text: Making minimal impact, by going with the tide?

definitions.text: Making minimal impact, by going with the tide?

parts.words: Making minimal impact, by going with the tide?
parts.note: a tiny quantity lost in a vast sea makes no difference, and literally it would be carried by the tide

explanation.surface: Someone who conforms makes little impression on events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going with the tide' suggests conformity, but literally a droplet in the sea moves with it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an amount too small to matter compared with the whole.

clue.text: Victim of jealousy doomed by more hearsay

definitions.text: Victim of jealousy doomed by more hearsay

parts.words: Victim of jealousy doomed by more hearsay
parts.note: 'more' heard aloud is Moor, Othello, who killed his wife on the strength of Iago's lies, the hearsay

explanation.surface: Someone envied is ruined by further gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' stands for its sound-alike Moor: Othello, Shakespeare's Moor, strangles his wife after Iago's false rumours.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello's wife in Shakespeare's play is murdered by her jealous husband.

clue.text: Lay about subordinate neglecting English? Keep it clean!

indicators.note: one word placed around another, so the letters of Lay go about the inner piece

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: leaving something out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: someone under another is subordinate to them

explanation.surface: A slacker loafs about with a junior employee, urged to keep things decent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay about' looks like a loafer; it is LAY wrapped around a subordinate minus E. 'Keep it clean!' defines by what you do with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty clothes waiting to be washed are the things one sends off to keep clean.

clue.text: Going ahead, often having to be patient, seriously?

definitions.text: often having to be patient, seriously?
definitions.meaning: a seriously ill patient is often in hospital

explanation.surface: Progress often requires serious patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patient' seems an adjective about waiting, but it is a hospital patient, found on wards.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in direction or time, continuing ahead, is its everyday meaning.

clue.text: Check on drivers — not a choice selection

indicators.note: a selection is a portion picked out, so the letters are taken from within the words

explanation.surface: A control on motorists that offers no options.
explanation.walkthrough: A tacho, short for tachograph, records lorry drivers' hours and speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tachograph monitors professional drivers' hours, keeping a check on them.

clue.text: Fruit dish penpal excitedly tucks into

indicators.note: one thing tucked inside another, so the shuffled letters go inside the dish

parts.note: a pie is a baked dish

indicators.note: an excited state stirs the letters into disorder

explanation.surface: A friend from abroad eagerly eats a fruity dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penpal excitedly' is the anagram; 'dish' is the pie that the shuffled letters are tucked into.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical fruit with spiky skin and sweet yellow flesh.

clue.text: Should there be a turning at the end of this road?

definitions.text: Should there be a turning at the end of this road?

parts.words: Should there be a turning at the end of this road?
parts.note: a dead-end street ends in a turning circle and has no further turning off it

explanation.surface: A motorist asks whether a turn-off lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The question seems to ask about a turn-off, but the road has no exit, only space to turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed street with no through route, where vehicles turn round at the end.

clue.text: Lacking preparation, bluff — or freeze?

parts.note: doing something cold means doing it without warming up
a front is a show put on to deceive, a bluff

explanation.surface: Unprepared, should one put on an act or simply freeze?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a weather front of cold air may bring freezing conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary of advancing chilly air, in weather terms, can bring a freeze.

clue.text: Ruin one local party

parts.note: 'un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'
a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood party is spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo someone is to bring about their downfall or ruin.

clue.text: Replacing parts for Beetle may be a headache

indicators.note: the two halves of the word swap places, one part moved from the front to the back

parts.note: to beetle is to project or overhang, as beetling brows do

explanation.surface: Fitting spares to a VW Beetle can be a real pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' suggests the car, but it is the verb to overhang; OVER moves to the end of OVERHANG.
explanation.definitionFit: The morning after heavy drinking brings a hangover, which may be a headache.

clue.text: Is artist able to cope? Be right to contribute capital

parts.note: can means able to
taken as written
RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: Questioning whether a painter can manage, with a call to contribute money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but is the capital city of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's capital city is Canberra.

clue.text: New rule's introduced in type of tennis

parts.note: a law is a rule; the 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: A new regulation is brought into one form of tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawn tennis is the original name of the game played on grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawn tennis is the formal name for tennis played on a grass court.

clue.text: Exclude three articles for woolly material

parts.note: to bar is to exclude
a, the and a are English articles, indefinite and definite
a, the and a are English articles, indefinite and definite
a, the and a are English articles, indefinite and definite

explanation.surface: Ban three items of clothing made of wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests garments, but means grammatical articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Barathea is a fine woollen fabric used for suits and uniforms.

clue.text: Notice this writer's keeping first reference to lust decent

parts.note: to see is to notice

indicators.note: holding something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: my is the possessive of the writer speaking

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Observe that the writer is restraining their first mention of desire, to be proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly behaviour is proper and in good taste.

clue.text: No, this is difficult

parts.note: the expression 'no ...' with this word attached means something is hard work

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a task is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'no picnic' means something difficult, so prefixing 'No' makes this word mean hard.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing to eat outdoors stands for something easy, hence the idiom 'no picnic' for a hard task.

clue.text: The result of laying on a good spread

definitions.text: The result of laying on a good spread

parts.words: The result of laying on a good spread
parts.note: providing a lavish meal puts weight on the diners, who spread at the waist

explanation.surface: What comes of hosting a generous meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' is both a feast and a widening waistline.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that adds weight to the eater is described this way.

clue.text: Allow bishop and another piece to be taken

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a rook is another chess piece, the castle

explanation.surface: In chess, a bishop and a second piece are captured.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture misleads: 'to be taken' is filler, and 'Allow' defines the verb to brook.
explanation.definitionFit: To brook something, usually in the negative, is to tolerate or permit it.

clue.text: County has vital elements of education introduced

indicators.note: brought inside, so one piece goes in the other

parts.note: something key is vital
the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, are the basics of schooling; two Rs stand for them here

explanation.surface: A county with the basics of schooling brought in.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerry is a county in south-west Ireland; the 'three Rs' are the basics of education.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerry is a county in the south-west of Ireland.

clue.text: He may well have rows with his neighbours

definitions.text: He may well have rows with his neighbours

parts.words: He may well have rows with his neighbours
parts.note: 'rows' suggests quarrels but means rowing, done alongside crew-mates in the boat

explanation.surface: A man who often argues with those living next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' rhymes with 'cows' in the surface but is read as rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower in a crew pulls an oar beside those seated next to him.

clue.text: Artist is right — objectively, I got into change of direction

indicators.note: entered, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: to veer is to change direction
me is the object form of I

explanation.surface: A painter is right that I was caught in a sudden swerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objectively' signals the grammatical object case: I becomes ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was a Dutch painter of the seventeenth century.

clue.text: Herb used in browning, extremely spicy

parts.note: a tan is browning of the skin

indicators.note: the extreme ends of the word, its first and last letters, are taken

explanation.surface: A herb used to brown food, very hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tansy is a yellow-flowered aromatic plant once used in cooking.

clue.text: It's inevitable, yet I can't worry about onset of reform

indicators.note: placed around, so the shuffled letters surround the inner letter
to worry something is to work it about, so the letters are disturbed
the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone resigned to change says they still can't fret about reform beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worry' turns YET I CANT into CETAINTY, placed 'about' the R from reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bound to happen is a sure thing; 'it's a certainty' means it's inevitable.
